reader_question: Who pays the nation’s health care bill?
grade_line: Documented: the federal government’s National Health Expenditure Accounts
title: Private insurance, Medicare and Medicaid together paid 70 percent of the nation’s health care bill in 2024, up from 21 percent in 1960.
measure_line: National health spending by who paid, as a share of each year’s total, United States, 1960 to 2024
notes: Medicare and Medicaid began paying in 1966.

All other sources of funds adds up out-of-pocket spending, the Children’s Health Insurance Program, the Departments of Defense and Veterans Affairs, other third-party payers and programs, and public health activity and investment.
alt: Stacked bands of the nation’s health spending by who paid, as shares of each year from 1960 to 2024. Private insurance paid 21 percent in 1960 and 31 percent in 2024; Medicare and Medicaid, which began in 1966, paid 21 and 18 percent in 2024; all other sources, out of pocket the largest, fell from 79 percent to 30.
